Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer

---
name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

# After a hand change to the setup, nothing invites a check: options

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28. Branch `claude/setup-changed-entry` in this worktree, cut from jusprin-newui a684aee37d. No code changed. Kenneth picks; nothing gets built before that.

## The problem in one paragraph

The agent recorded a plan for a PLA wall hook. The person then switched the filament to Generic ABS from the header chip. The setup card gained "⚠ Plan needs another look · Generic ABS @System", Print turned back into Slice, and the agent said nothing. The person pressed Slice; the slice finished with ABS, and the agent still said nothing. The agent only answered once the person typed "Is it still fine to print like this?", and that answer was very good. Two smaller defects: the warning left the card while the agent was still working, before the person had chosen anything, and "@System" is a preset-library word the person does not know.

## How I checked it

- **Saved record of this morning's run.** The UX walkthrough (critique frames 2C-01 to 2C-05) left its project state on disk: `current-state.json` of project `p-e2b6763d55d34718-…` in that session's scratch data folder. It shows the exact sequence:
  - 12:58:43: a change row `{actor: person, kind: preset, location: filament, label: "Generic ABS @System"}`.
  - 12:59:11: a grey chat note, posted when the filament menu closed: "Filament is now Generic ABS. Heat and cooling follow ABS; walls and infill unchanged. Slice again when ready."
  - 13:00:25: the person's question, then seven tool calls in one turn.
  - 13:00:47: the sixth call, `setup_record`, with the **same headline** and the Material decision rewritten to "Filament switched by the person to Generic ABS … recommended over ABS here" (that is, PLA or PETG recommended instead).
  - 13:00:50: the answer text with its three choices.

  The plan is now `validity: current`, so the card's warning was cleared by that mid-turn `setup_record`, before the person had chosen anything.
- **My own run.** I launched a scratch copy of the same build with a scratch data folder. The request to control its window was declined, so I could not drive it, and I stopped it and deleted that data folder. **So I have no screenshots of my own.** The evidence is the saved record above plus the code paths below. The verification after the fix still needs screen control or the instrumented-page route (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL`).

## Where each piece lives

| Piece | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Flag set | `Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:130` `on_edit` → `ProjectStateDocument::mark_plan_needs_reassessment` (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:1126`) | Any edit whose actor is not the in-app agent (the person, Undo or Redo, an external MCP client) sets `validity = needs_reassessment` and `invalidatedBy = edit.label`. Each edit overwrites the reason, so after several edits the card shows only the last one. |
| Reason text | `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3027` | For a preset change the label is the raw preset name (`Generic ABS @System`). `location` (`filament` / `printer` / `process`) is stored but the card does not use it. |
| Card line | `AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx:111` `planNote` | Shows `Plan needs another look · <invalidatedBy>` whenever a headline exists and the plan is flagged. It never looks at `working`; nothing on the page hides it while the agent works. `shortPreset` strips " @…" from the presets line but `planNote` does not use it. |
| Flag cleared | `setup_record` with a headline (tool guide, row `setup_record`) | Any headline clears it, the same one included. The skill tells the model to do this "in this reply". That instruction is why the warning vanished before the person chose. |
| Skill attached | `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2850` (first request of a turn) and `:3140` (on a tool result within a turn) | `project-setup-changed` is attached when `setup_unchecked` is true: a purpose is recorded and the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup saved as checked (`setup_in_force`, which covers only those four). Attaching it saves the current setup as checked (`begin_stream`, `:2743`), so the skill fires once per change. It needs a request, and a request needs a turn. |
| No turn after the person's slice | `AgentHost::slice_ended` (`:1792`) | Only a `slice_start` the in-app model called gets a "The slice of Plate 1 finished." note and a new turn. A slice the person started returns early ("the person watches their own in the status row"). Its warnings and failures reach the model only on the next request. |
| Chat note on a filament change | `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:456` `on_filament_visit` → `AgentHost::post_note` | One grey line per menu visit. It starts no turn and is never sent to the model. It ends with "Slice again when ready.", which nudges the person to slice without the agent. The printer chip and the plate type post no such line. |

Two facts that bear on the options:

- **App-started turns are not only for slices the model started.** In the code today, a turn also starts after the person opens a file (the agent speaks first), after the person presses Save preset on a proposal (`on_proposal_saved`), after Undo on a saved-preset receipt, after a calibration handover, and when a calibration project is reopened. So a turn started by the person's own action already has precedent. The rule as passed to me ("only for a slice the model started") looks out of date. **Kenneth, please confirm which rule stands.**
- **The flag and the skill react to different changes.** The flag goes up on *any* hand edit, such as a wall-count change or moving an object. The skill fires only when one of the four setup items changes. After a hand edit to a single setting, the card says "needs another look" and the next turn carries no skill that explains the flag. The only trace is `plan.validity` in the request's workspace block.

## Options

A and B are alternative ways in; pick at most one. C and D fix the two smaller defects and go with either.

### A. "Check the plan" on the card's warning line (recommended way in)

- **What the person sees:** the warning line gets a link button, the way "Previous estimates · not current" already carries "Recompute":
  `⚠ You changed the filament to Generic ABS · Check plan`
  It shows from the moment of the change, stays through a manual slice (frame 2C-03), and goes when the plan is re-recorded. Pressing it posts a message in the person's name, as the print-issue chip's Ask AI does, for example "Check the plan with this change." The agent then answers as in frame 2C-05.
- **Where it lives:** mostly on the page. `SetupCard` gets the action, as `onCompute` does, and `App.tsx` sends the message through the normal send path. On the host, one condition changes: the first request also attaches `project-setup-changed` when the plan is flagged, not only when the four-item setup moved. That closes the gap for single-setting edits.
- **Model cost:** none unless pressed. A press costs one normal turn, about what the walkthrough's answer turn took: 7 tool calls, so 8 requests. At roughly 10k tokens of prompt and tools per request, plus history, that is on the order of 100–250k input tokens, mostly cached. That is an estimate; I have no usage figures.
- **Downside:** the person still has to notice the line and choose to press it. But it is the one place they are already looking (frame 2C-02), and it answers the critique's literal complaint: "'Needs another look' by whom? There is no button."

### B. The app starts a turn by itself

Two moments it could fire:

- **B1, right after the change** (when the filament menu closes, a printer is picked, or the plate type changes). The agent speaks within seconds, as it does after a file opens.
- **B2, when a slice the person started finishes while the plan is flagged.** This is the moment of risk in frame 2C-03. It is `slice_ended`'s note-and-turn, extended to the person's slice, only while the plan is flagged and once per flag.

- **What the person sees:** B1: a reply after every flagged change, even a deliberate one. B2: nothing until they slice, then "The slice finished with Generic ABS; on your open A1 mini that risks…" with choices.
- **Where it lives:** host. B1 hooks `on_filament_visit` and the printer and plate paths. B2 extends `AgentHost::slice_ended` to slices the person started.
- **Model cost:** B1 spends a turn on every flagged hand change, including several in a row (the turns queue). B2 spends at most one turn per flagged state, and only if the person slices without asking.
- **Downsides:** B1 talks over a person who is still editing and cannot tell a deliberate choice from an experiment. B2 speaks only after the G-code exists, so it reads as a correction after the fact. Both turn the app's own state into model turns that nobody asked for. That is the part your rule is about.

### C. Keep the warning until the person has decided (do this with A or B)

- **The cause, from the saved record:** the skill says "record the plan again with setup_record **in this reply** … the same headline if the plan still holds". So the model re-recorded mid-turn, with the same headline, while it was recommending that the person switch back. Any headline clears the flag.
- **Fix, situational text only (no code):** reword the skill's last bullet along these lines: "If you recommend a change the person has to choose, ask first and record the plan after they answer; the card keeps its mark until then. If the plan holds as is, record it in this reply." This is in line with "situational guidance from state channels": it is skill text, attached only in this situation.
- **The reset rule it needs:** once the skill has fired, the setup counts as checked, so the turn that carries the person's answer gets no skill. Without one more change, the flag could stay up forever if the model forgets to record. Host fix: while the plan is flagged, every first request carries the skill. This is the same condition as in A, so A and C share one host change. The flag then clears only through `setup_record`, which is the existing single rule.
- **Cost:** the skill text (about 250 tokens) on each request while the flag is up; usually one or two turns.

### D. Name the change in the person's words (do this regardless)

- **Today:** `Plan needs another look · Generic ABS @System`.
- **Proposed:** `You changed the filament to Generic ABS`. The same pattern covers the printer, the process ("print settings") and the plate type. A single setting reads `You changed Wall loops to 5`, Undo reads `You undid <step>`, and an MCP client reads `<client> changed …`. The words come from fields the change row already stores (`kind`, `location`, `label`, `to`) with " @…" stripped. They are built on the host when the flag is set, so the card and the model read the same words.
- **Also:** when several edits happen, keep the most significant one rather than the last (printer over filament over process over a single setting). A printer switch cascades into filament and process changes, and today the card would name the process.
- **Also:** drop "Slice again when ready." from the filament note while a plan is recorded. It points the person at Slice instead of at the check.
- **Where it lives:** host (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment` callers and `StatusRow::on_filament_visit`); the page only shows the text. **Model cost:** none.

## Recommendation

A + C + D. A gives the person an invitation exactly where the warning already is, at no model cost unless they want the check. C makes the warning mean "the plan has not caught up yet" until the person has actually decided. D removes "@System" and says what changed. The host change that A and C share ("attach the skill while the plan is flagged") also covers single-setting edits, which today raise the flag without the skill.

If Kenneth wants the agent to speak up without being asked, B2 is the version to add on top. It fires at most once, and only when a slice is made against a flagged plan. I would not do B1.

## Test plan once chosen (multi-turn, as the brief asks)

A host-level test drives this sequence through the agent host with a stub model. The scripted replies choose which tools are called; no live model is involved.

1. Record a plan.
2. The person changes the filament: the plan is flagged, the reason reads in the person's words (D), and no turn starts (or exactly one, under B).
3. The person slices: the flag stays.
4. The next turn (the A button or a typed message): its first request carries the skill.
5. That turn asks a question without `setup_record`: the flag stays (C).
6. The person answers: the answer turn's first request carries the skill again, and its `setup_record` clears the flag.
7. One more turn: no skill, no flag.

Plus a page test for the button and the wording. Then the real app with screenshots of the 2C frames, for which I need screen control of a scratch copy (declined this time) or the instrumented-page route.

`write_screen_capture` / `blit_screen` in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` photograph the desktop through `wxScreenDC`. With the screen locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` prints a line) every PNG is a blank ~2.8 KB file and no check fails.

For anything drawn inside the GL canvas (ImGui overlays, the tool strip, bubbles) read the frame back instead: `prepare_canvas().render()`, then `glReadBuffer(GL_FRONT)` and `glReadPixels` over `get_canvas_size()`, flip vertically into a `wxImage`, save as PNG. Worked on 2026-10-08 with the screen locked and the window inactive; needs `#include <glad/gl.h>`. Native notifications drawn by Orca are in the same frame, so they appear too. Web views still need `capture_web_view`.

Side effect of an inactive window: Orca's `NotificationManager::update_notifications` returns early, so closed popups are never retired and `get_notification_count()` only grows.

Before this change it fired only when `setup_unchecked_change` (printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the checked setup) or after a restore.    std::string plan_doubt_reason(const Workspace::WorkspaceEdit& edit)
   {

                            : "by " + (edit.client.empty() ? std::string("another app") : edit.client);
       const auto short_preset = [](const std::string& name) { return name.substr(0, name.find(" @")); };
       switch (edit.kind) {
       case Workspace::EditKind::Preset: {
           const std::string what = edit.location == "printer"  ? "Printer"
                                  : edit.location == "filament" ? "Filament" : "Print settings";
           return what + " changed to " + short_preset(edit.label) + " " + by;
       }
       case Workspace::EditKind::Setting:
           return edit.label + " changed" + (edit.after.empty() ? std::string() : " to " + edit.after) + " " + by;
       case Workspace::EditKind::Undo: return edit.label.empty() ? "Undone " + by : edit.label + " undone " + by;
       case Workspace::EditKind::Redo: return edit.label.empty() ? "Redone " + by : edit.label + " redone " + by;
